source_snapshot.procedure: Toggle by physical button, WebUI on/off, open remote KVM, issue `ipmitool chassis identify`, and visually inspect behavior/color.
source_snapshot.criteria: Manual and WebUI on are blue; manual off is off; criterion 4 incorrectly says off when WebUI turns on; remote use expects flashing.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO because physical LED observation is human-only.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: BLOCKED for the WebUI on/off contradiction and KVM-versus-identify flash cause.

old_problem: The prior review treated a local wording error and two adjacent possible flash causes as requiring a new owner decision, even though procedure order supplies the WebUI-off action and full coverage can isolate KVM and IPMI rather than choosing one.
disposition_reason: Procedure step 5 explicitly presses WebUI UID off and step 6 checks it, so Criteria 4's second `turning on` is bound in the review layer to that off transition while the protected text remains unchanged. The final sequence contains both KVM and `chassis identify`; testing KVM-only and identify-only as separate restored phases preserves both possible source intents and establishes causality without deleting coverage.
decision_basis: Direct inspection covered XLSX row 813, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2 and the historical record.
The preceding procedure action is an explicit WebUI-off command, providing a local, traceable resolution for the repeated word in criterion 4.

Intel IPMI 2.0 defines Chassis Identify as a bounded physical identification indication, with default 15-second timeout when no interval is supplied and an implementation-selected mechanism such as blinking lights.
ED physical/visual and ED-31 rules require a human to observe the real LED and WebUI; command success alone cannot pass the case.

test_case.test_name: Verify UID synchronization for physical button, WebUI, KVM and bounded IPMI identify
test_case.purpose: Verify on the exact chassis that the physical UID indicator and rendered WebUI state remain synchronized for manual on/off and WebUI on/off, then independently characterize the source-required KVM flashing behavior and the IPMI Chassis Identify indication, returning to idle between every phase.
required_package: Chassis/board/BMC firmware UID specification and physical LED/button locator
Project state matrix for physical color, steady/flashing pattern, WebUI label/icon, KVM behavior and identify duration/tolerance
Actual BMC WebUI/Remote KVM access and protected IPMI credentials
Reviewed private UID script revision if used, plus human camera/timestamp evidence and a verified BMC-to-chassis serial mapping
test_case.test_command: Begin with UID physically and in WebUI OFF. Run four separately restored phases: (1) human presses the UID button once for ON and once for OFF; (2) human uses actual WebUI ON then OFF; (3) with identify inactive, open KVM only, observe the source-required flashing state, close KVM and restore OFF; (4) with KVM closed, issue the approved bounded `ipmitool chassis identify <seconds>` form, observe the implementation-specific physical/WebUI indication through timeout, and explicitly turn it off if needed. Capture physical and WebUI evidence after every transition.
test_case.expected_result: Manual ON and WebUI ON each show the correct steady blue physical LED and matching WebUI state; manual OFF and WebUI OFF each show physical/WebUI OFF. The isolated KVM phase produces the source-required flash only according to the project KVM contract and returns idle when closed. The isolated IPMI phase produces the approved identify indication for the bounded interval and deasserts. All observations belong to the verified chassis and no phase contaminates the next.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires all four checkpoints with action timestamps, actual physical visual evidence, matching WebUI/KVM/command evidence and verified restoration. A remote status or completion code cannot replace color/flash observation. FAIL includes wrong color/pattern/state, physical-WebUI disagreement, unexpected KVM behavior, identify timeout/cleanup error, wrong target or stuck UID. Unsupported KVM coupling may be N/A only when authoritative Project SPEC proves it, not by omission.
safety_gate: Human alone presses the physical button and certifies LED color/steady/flash/off appearance
Verify serial/location identity before every remote control and protect credentials
Do not overlap KVM and IPMI phases; restore physical and WebUI OFF after each
Use an explicitly bounded identify interval; do not leave force-identify active
Stop on wrong chassis, stuck state, UI/physical mismatch or lost BMC/KVM access; no automatic retry
expected_evidence: Chassis serial/location, BMC/firmware, UID state matrix and physical locator
Timestamped physical video/photos and WebUI screenshots for manual ON/OFF
Timestamped WebUI action plus physical/WebUI ON/OFF correlation
KVM-only session and visual flash/return-to-idle evidence
Bounded IPMI command/output, physical/WebUI identify pattern and timeout/off evidence
Final physical and WebUI OFF plus audit/health logs
test_case.recovery: Use the verified WebUI or local button to return UID to OFF. If a bounded IPMI indication fails to expire, issue only the approved identify-off action while the operator observes the same chassis. Preserve the mismatch and audit evidence and escalate before retrying or resetting BMC.

source_conflict.preserved_original_conflict: Criteria 4 repeats `turning on`, and KVM plus identify precede one final observation.
source_conflict.resolution: Bind criterion 4 to procedure's immediately preceding OFF action; split KVM-only and identify-only into independent phases with restoration.

blocked.reason: Every source control and visual outcome now has a distinct causal checkpoint; model-specific appearance/timing are Project Configuration.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Exact UID appearance/timing/state matrix, verified chassis mapping, BMC/KVM versions, protected access and script applicability.

external_authorities.title: Intel IPMI v2.0 — Chassis Identify Command
external_authorities.use: Defines implementation-chosen physical indication, bounded interval/default timeout and explicit off/force semantics.
